tagline: A desert road reaches a salt marsh and remains of borax mining.
intro: Saline Valley Road is a BLM Back Country Byway through desert terrain, with a dry lake and a salt marsh on the valley floor. FHWA describes a four-wheel-drive route and highlights the marsh’s plant and animal life amid sparse surroundings. Most of the valley became part of Death Valley National Park in 1994, after BLM administration.

Mining once made transport across this basin a commercial problem: salt traveled by wagon before an aerial tram was built from 1911 to 1913 over the Inyo Mountains to Owens Valley. Its construction and operation proved ruinously expensive for the Saline Valley Salt Company. At the warm springs, recreational users began constructing tubs in the 1950s; the Park Service later developed a management plan with the Timbisha Shoshone Tribe among its cooperating agencies.
The northern approach comes from Big Pine over North Pass. Warm Springs Road reaches the springs in the valley’s northeast corner; farther south lies the dry lake, with dunes to its north.

moments.title: North Pass approach
moments.text: Saline Valley’s northern road approach comes from Big Pine over North Pass. After Hurricane Hilary damaged park roads in August 2023, Inyo County repaired this approach and the Park Service announced its reopening that November.

moments.title: Saline Valley Warm Springs
moments.text: Warm Springs Road, also called Painted Rock Road, leads to the valley’s three main warm springs. Recreational users began developing soaking tubs and art installations in the 1950s. The site passed from BLM to the Park Service in 1994. The 2019 management plan proposed retaining existing tubs at Lower Spring and Palm Spring while leaving Upper Spring undeveloped.

moments.title: Salt marsh and mining traces
moments.text: At the west end of the dry lake, a perennial stream from Hunter Canyon feeds a salt marsh. Shallow pits near Saline Valley Road remain from borax mining. Salt mining began at the lake’s south end in 1903 and continued into the 1930s.

practical: North Pass approach: The Park Service advises checking current road status before travel. (checked 2026-10-20)
